title: The Relationship between Car Ownership and Employment Rate in New York State
text:
In the State of New York, car dependency has become an important fact within the work culture for many New Yorkers across the state. The question this project will look at is what is the relationship between car ownership and the employment rate in different parts of the state? Will we find places that have high car ownership also to have greater job opportunities and employment rate?
If so, how can this research be used to help those who don’t own a car, still have access to job opportunities across the state? The potential answers to this question could also help explain how car ownership is crucial for working in the modern era today.
The goal of this Project
The data being used to with in this project can all be found within NY’s data. gov website
Code: The code associated with the project is well organized and easy to follow. Demonstrates mastery of R graphics and functions.
Data: The underlying data are publicly accessible via the web and downloaded/accessed within the Rmd script. If you want to use your own data, you must make it available on a website (e.g. Figshare) so that others are able to re-run your code.

library(tidyverse)
library(leaflet)
library(kableExtra)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(widgetframe_widgets_dir = 'widgets' ) 
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache=TRUE)  # cache the results for quick compiling




n=20
data=data.frame(x=runif(n,-180,180),
                y=runif(n,-60,60),
                size = runif(n, 5, 20),
                category = factor(
                  sample(letters[1:5], n, replace = TRUE)
                  ),
                value = rnorm(n))

  slice(1:10) %>% #show only 1:n rows
  kable(digits=2,align="c")%>% #make table and round to two digits
